Subject: Evaluating your platform vs. competitors – a few specific questions

Hi there,

We’re a mid-sized B2B SaaS company (about 80 quota-carrying reps, 25 SDRs) currently evaluating sales engagement platforms. We’ve done a short trial of your Essentials tier about a year ago, and a lot seems to have changed since then, so I’d like to sanity-check a few points before we invest more time.

Our current stack is Salesforce (core CRM), Gong, and Outreach for a subset of the team. We’re considering consolidating onto a single platform for sequencing, basic dialer, email tracking, and reporting across both SDRs and AEs. We’d probably start with ~90 seats and scale up to 120 over the next 12–18 months.

A few things we’re thinking about:

1) Core stance on features
From what I can see on your website and a quick skim of your docs, it looks like advanced sequencing, multi-channel cadences, and some level of AI-driven send-time optimization are pretty much table stakes across the market now. My assumption is that these are bundled in your base plans by default – we’re not really interested in add-on pricing for what most tools treat as standard. If that assumption is off, let me know, but we’re unlikely to pay separately for basic functionality.

2) Integrations & data model
We are on Salesforce Enterprise and need a fairly tight, bi-directional sync (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities) without a lot of custom engineering. Our RevOps team is small, so heavy custom build-outs are a non-starter. I didn’t see anything in your public docs that clearly states whether you support writing back task outcomes and email engagement at the account/opportunity level out of the box, or if that requires custom work.

We’re also trying to understand how your system handles ownership conflicts (e.g., SDR vs. AE) and routing rules when multiple people are touching the same account.

3) Pricing & packaging
We’ve already received a quote from NovaReach (one of your obvious competitors). They’re coming in ~20% lower than the ballpark pricing that one of your SDRs mentioned on a call last week, for roughly comparable functionality on paper.

To be blunt, we’re not going to pay a significant premium just for UI polish or marginal differences in workflow. If the reality is that everyone in this space is offering essentially the same capabilities, we’ll probably default to the cheaper option.

That said, our team did generally prefer your interface during the earlier trial, and the analytics looked stronger. If there’s a substantive difference in how your product handles reporting, Salesforce sync, or governance (permissions, audit trails, compliance), I’d be interested to hear that – but I need specifics, not just generic marketing language.

4) Commercial terms
We strongly prefer monthly or, at worst, quarterly terms for the first year. Locking into a full annual contract up front is a tough sell internally given that we already have Outreach in place for part of the org. My expectation (and please correct me if I’m mistaken) is that most vendors in this category are moving toward more flexible, cancel-anytime monthly plans, especially for deals at our size.

Next steps
If you can:
- Clarify which of the above assumptions are correct/incorrect,
- Outline how your Salesforce integration and reporting meaningfully differ from NovaReach and similar tools,
- And give me a realistic sense of pricing/terms for ~90 seats (SDRs + AEs),

then I can decide whether to push this forward to a more formal evaluation and involve our VP Sales and RevOps lead.

Looking forward to your response.

Best,
Laura
Director of Sales Operations
BrightPath Systems
